evidence.quote: Schmid-Schoenbein Lab Principal Investigator: Geert Schmid-Schoenbein Website | gschmid@ucsd.edu
AUTODIGESTION Schmid-Schoenbein Lab Principal Investigator: Geert Schmid-Schoenbein
Microcirculation Laboratory Center for Autodigestion Innovation
Our Mission Investigate and minimize Autodigestion as mechanism for human diseases, aging, and death.
Pancreatic digestive enzymes have escaped the gastrointestinal tract and degraded your own tissues besides our food.

Develop new bioengineering tools to identify cellular and molecular mechanisms that lead to tissue and organ dysfunction by pancreatic digestive enzymes. Design new interventions to minimize cell and tissue dysfunctions and destruction initiated and caused by digestive enzymes.

The Microcirculation Laboratory at UC San Diego was founded in 1967 by the late Benjamin W. Zweifach, one of the imminent teachers of Bioengineering and Microcirculation in the twentieth century. In 1979, Geert W. Schmid-Schönbein assumed the directorship of the laboratory.

A premise of the laboratory is that diseases are manifest in the microcirculation years before they become evident at the clinical level. The study of microcirculation is a cornerstone for the integration of molecular, genetic, and cellular phenomena with the dynamics in living tissue and whole organs. Microcirculation is a key to analyzing the origin and progression of disease.

Microcirculation Laboratory Research Summary Aging by Autodigestion A Fundamental Mechanism for Loss of Cell and Tissue Function over a Lifetime Autodigestion in Sepsis and Hemorrhagic Shock Multiorgan Failure by Digestive Enzymes Metabolic Disease and Receptor Cleavage Loss of Receptor Signalling by Digestive Protease and Secondary Proteases. The Immature Intestine of Infants A Risk for Autodigestion & Potential Connection to Necrotizing Enterocolitis and Autism
